description: MCP server: 5,000 years of military strategy and philosophy — Napoleon, Sun Tzu, Clausewitz, Alexander, Hannibal, Genghis Khan, Shaka Zulu, Caesar. All public domain.

tools.name: napoleon_maxims
tools.description: Napoleon's Maxims of War (1831, public domain), by category (strategy, tactics, logistics, leadership, intelligence or all) or by number. Use when someone wants a maxim or a modern reading of one. maxim_number above 0 returns that maxim or an error if it does not exist; otherwise category filters, and an unrecognised category returns an empty list. Returns the commander, source, count and the maxims, each with a modern application. Read-only.

tools.name: sun_tzu
tools.description: Chapters of Sun Tzu's The Art of War (13 chapters, public domain), or a search across verses for a concept such as deception, intelligence or terrain. Use when someone asks what Sun Tzu said about a topic. chapter above 0 returns that chapter or an error if it does not exist; concept searches the verse text for a match. Returns the chapter or the matching verses with chapter and verse numbers. Read-only.

tools.name: commander_doctrine
tools.description: Doctrine of a historical commander (napoleon, alexander, hannibal, genghis, shaka, caesar, sun_tzu, clausewitz or frederick) with principles and sources. Use when someone asks how a particular commander approached war or leadership. An unknown name returns an error listing the available commanders. Returns the doctrine and its public-domain source. Historical summaries, not operational guidance. Read-only.

tools.name: apply_strategy
tools.description: Apply a strategic lens (competition, leadership, intelligence, resources, operations or psychology) to a problem and return a framework of key questions drawn from public-domain military literature. Use when someone wants a structured way to think through a hard problem. An unrecognised lens uses the competition framework and lens_applied says so. commanders is accepted as a comma-separated list or all. Returns the problem, the lens, the framework, a source and a note. Analytical frameworks only, not operational recommendations; historical strategy needs contextual adaptation. Read-only.

tools.name: public_domain_library
tools.description: Catalogue of public-domain works on strategy, philosophy, leadership and history, including African and Mongol sources, with author, date and themes. Use when someone asks what to read. domain filters the catalogue; an unrecognised domain returns an empty list. Returns the works and a note that all are public domain. A curated list, not a full library. Read-only.
